newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up on short covering.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps firmed at midday on Monday on short covering by players who feel that the market has bottomed in the absence of fresh indicators, traders said.
"Gas oil is firm this afternoon on some short covering I think because the fundamentals are still the same and there a lot of oil out there," one trader said.
August swaps were indicated at $21.30/$21.40 per barrel, up from Friday's $20.95/$21.05. August traded at $21.30 earlier in the day compared to a traded high of $20.05 late Friday, brokers said.
July was actively traded up one short coverings with deals done at $20.40, $20.50 and $20.55 and was last quoted at $20.55/$20.65, compared to Friday's $19.90/$20.00, they said.
As a result of the sharp increase to July values, the July/August time spread narrowed substantially to trade at minus 75 cents from $1.00 on Friday.
September was quoted at $22.10/$22.25, up about 15 cents from Friday which has also cut the August/September spread to value at about minus 85 cents from Friday's minus $1.00 per barrel value.

Traders saud tge firmer prices are also due to the stronger crude where August Brent last traded up 17 cents to $18.26 after putting on 13 cents on Friday to end at $18.09 on London's International Petroleum Exchange.

But others say the upside is limited due to the persistent prompt physical overhang which has forced sellers to offer cargoes at lower prices throughout last week in an effort to get rid of prompt cargoes.

On Friday a 30,000 tonne cargo was offered at $148.50 per tonne ($19.93 per barrel) and a 150,000 barrel cargo at $20.00--the lower offer being the first time in about three years that gas oil was offered below the $20.00 mark.
Although a buyer emerged for these cargoes but no deal was struck as the two parties could not agree on terms.
Traders said they expect similar offers to made later Monday which will continue to weigh down on prices in the absence of fresh regional demand.
Fuel oil swaps are steady with August and September last quoted at $98.25/$99.00, down from Friday's $98.50/$99.00.
